name: ZX Rallye Raid
hook: Citroën won four Dakars in a car shaped like a family hatchback, with its engine sitting where the back seat should be.
story:
From a distance it looks like a shopping car. A three-door Citroën ZX, the kind you park outside a bakery. Then it comes over a dune flat out, and the shape stops making sense.

Open the door and look behind the seats. That is where the engine lives. A turbocharged 2.5-litre four sits sideways in the middle of the car, where the back seat should be. It drives all four wheels. The hatchback body is only a costume, cut from carbon fibre and Kevlar.

The recipe was not new. Peugeot had already won the Dakar with a mid-engined 405 built along the same lines. Then the idea moved across the family, to Citroën, under a new badge.

At the wheel was Ari Vatanen, with Bruno Berglund beside him. They won the 1991 Paris–Dakar. It was Vatanen's third Dakar win in a row, and his fourth in all.

And the costume kept winning. Pierre Lartigue took three more Dakars in it, in 1994, 1995 and 1996.
description: The ZX Rallye Raid was Citroën's works cross-country car of the early and mid 1990s. It wore the outline of the three-door ZX hatchback in carbon-fibre and Kevlar panels over a purpose-built chassis. A turbocharged 2.5-litre four sat transversely behind the cockpit and drove all four wheels. It grew out of Peugeot's 405 Turbo 16 raid car. The ZX won the Paris–Dakar in 1991, 1994, 1995 and 1996, and the FIA Cross-Country Rally World Cup every year from 1993 to 1997.
